mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods meeting both GDPC1 < -2% YoY and UNRATE > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of more than 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is followed by negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to heightened recession risk and lower consumer spending power.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE rises by more than 0.4pp in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output and profit pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during three-month stretches of INDPRO < -0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based demand contraction, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by more than 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is cut by at least 0.5 percentage points in a single FOMC cycle and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is below 3%, equity risk premia compress and growth expectations rise, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during FOMC cycles with at least a 0.5pp rate cut and CPIAUCSL < 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment gain (PAYEMS) below 50,000 new jobs for three consecutive months signals weak labor market momentum, which correlates with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to earnings downgrades.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during three-month stretches with PAYEMS < 50,000 monthly.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on relationship exists between rising real personal savings (RSAFS) and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as increased household savings can translate into future consumption and investment, boosting corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when RSAFS increases month-over-month.
